The headset mics come in through the [wireless rack](wireless-rack-x32.qmd) on **channels 7–12** (pack 1 → channel 7 … pack 6 →
channel 12). This page sets up **one channel properly (7)**, copies it to 8–12, and saves everything as a **scene**.

::: {.callout-warning}
Button names and menu paths here are from memory of the X32 (firmware 4.x) and are **unverified**: check them against
Behringer's X32 manual on the desk. The numbers are a sensible starting point for speech headsets, not rules. Use your ears.
:::

## 1. Start clean

1. Press **VIEW** on the **Scenes** section (top right), and save what's on the desk now as a backup scene (e.g. "before headsets"),
   so you can go back.
2. Select channel 7 (its **SEL** button). Make sure nothing odd is left on it from last time. The quickest way is to load a
   blank channel preset from the **Library** (step 6), or reset it in the channel's Utility menu.

## 2. Channel 7, step by step

Do these with **pack 7 switched on** and someone talking into the headset at their normal speaking level.

| Step | Where | Starting setting | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name and colour | **Config** page | "HS1" … "HS6", or the performer's name; one colour for all six | Easy to find on the scribble strips |
| Phantom (+48V) | Config / Gain | **Off** | The receivers don't need it |
| Gain | **GAIN** knob | Talking peaks around **−18 dBFS** (yellow-green, never red) | See [gain](../lessons/live-gain.qmd). Set the receiver's output level first, then the X32 gain |
| High-pass (low cut) | Gain page, **LOW CUT** | **On, 100–120 Hz** | Removes breath pops, handling and stage rumble. Speech has nothing useful down there |
| Gate | **GATE** | **Off** to start. If you need it: threshold just below quiet speech, range **−10 dB** (not full), attack fast, release ~**200 ms** | A full gate chops off words. A gentle "expander" style range is safer |
| EQ | **EQ** | Flat, then: cut **−2 to −3 dB around 250–400 Hz** (boxiness), gentle **+2 dB around 3–5 kHz** if words are unclear | Headsets sit close to the mouth and sound muddy. Cut before you boost. See [EQ](../lessons/live-eq.qmd) |
| Compressor | **DYNAMICS** | Ratio **3:1**, attack **10 ms**, release **100–150 ms** (or Auto), knee soft, threshold so loud speech gets **3–6 dB** of gain reduction, makeup gain to match | Evens out loud and quiet speakers. See [compression](../lessons/live-comp.qmd) |
| Sends | Mix bus sends | Monitor buses as needed, **pre-fader** | Performers hear themselves however the main fader moves |
| Main | **LR** on, fader at **0 dB** (unity) | | Then mix with the faders |
| DCA / mute group | Config / Home | All six on one **DCA** (e.g. "Headsets") | One fader turns all the headsets up or down |

Ring-out check: with all faders at their show positions, if a headset howls, pull **that** frequency down with a narrow EQ cut
(see [feedback](../lessons/live-feedback.qmd)), not the gain.

## 3. Copy channel 7 to channels 8–12

**Yes, you can copy settings from one channel to another.** Two ways:

**A. Copy / Paste (quickest)**

1. Select channel 7 (**SEL**).
2. Press **UTILITY** while the channel's screen is showing. Choose **Copy**. You can pick which parts to copy: tick EQ, dynamics,
   gate, sends and so on, and **leave out the name and gain** (each person's voice needs its own gain).
3. Select channel 8, press **UTILITY**, choose **Paste**.
4. Repeat for 9, 10, 11, 12.

**B. Channel preset (reusable next time)**

1. Select channel 7, press **VIEW** on the Library / Utility screen and open the **Channel** library.
2. **Save** it as "Headset".
3. Select each of 8–12 and **Load** "Headset". Choose which parts to load the same way (leave out gain).

The preset stays on the desk, so the next show you can load "Headset" onto any channel without starting again.

In **X32-Edit** (on a laptop) you can also right-click a channel strip and copy / paste.

After copying, **set each channel's gain on its own** with its performer talking (step 2, gain row), and rename 8–12.

## 4. Save the scene

1. Go to the **Scenes** screen (**VIEW** in the Scenes section).
2. Pick an empty slot, **Save**, name it e.g. "Headsets 7-12".
3. To bring it back later: Scenes → select it → **Load** (Go).

Check **Safes** (scene safes) on that screen if there are channels you *don't* want the scene to change when it loads, for example
a band on channels 1–6.

## 5. Every show

- [ ] Load the scene "Headsets 7-12".
- [ ] Wireless on, one pack at a time: talk, check its channel meter.
- [ ] Adjust gain per person (singers and quiet talkers are different).
- [ ] Mix with the DCA.

## Sources

- Behringer, *X32 Digital Mixer User Manual* (check the Utility / Copy and Library sections for your firmware).
- Starting values are general live-sound practice for speech, **unverified** against a specific source.
